SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: Sixteen participants' professions were classified as IT. Nineteen participants' professions were classified as artistic. Fifteen participants indicated their profession as "student" or "unemployed," and were not considered in the analysis specific to the professional occupations, but were included in all other analyses. The total sample size for 'all other analyses' is 16 + 19 + 15 = 50. The sample size for the 'IT' group is 16. The sample size for the 'artistic' group is 19.

ES.evidence_source: The text states that 'IT and Artistic groups did not differ in... general cognitive abilities as measured by the International Cognitive Ability Resource (ICAR) test', but it does not provide any Pearson r correlation coefficients between intelligence and creative achievement.

Measure IQ.evidence_source: IT and Artistic groups did not differ in age, level of education, or general cognitive abilities as measured by the International Cognitive Ability Resource (ICAR) test (Condon & Revelle, 2014; see Table 1).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the categorization of participants into professional groups: 16 in IT and 19 in artistic domains, with an additional 15 students/unemployed included in general analyses. It notes that the IT and Artistic groups did not differ in gender, age, education level, or general cognitive abilities, which were assessed using the International Cognitive Ability Resource (ICAR) test.
